## Exploratory data analysis

For this section graph and find statistics for each of your predictor variables vs the response. You do not need to look at the predictor variables individually

```{r}
#| include: false
long_data <- project2_merged |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(sanitation_access_pct, food_supply_kcal_per_person_day, 
             murder_deaths_per_100k, child_deaths_per_100k), 
    names_to  = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  )

make_plot <- function(var, ylab) {
  graph <- long_data |>
    filter(variable == var) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = Democracy, y = value, fill = Democracy)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.shape = 21, outlier.size = 2) +
    labs(title = paste(ylab, " by Democracy Status"), x = "Democracy Status", y = ylab, fill = "Group") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
  graph
}
make_table <- function(var) { 
  table <- project2_merged |>
    summarise(
      n      = sum(!is.na(.data[[var]])),
      mean   = mean(.data[[var]],   na.rm = TRUE),
      median = median(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE),
      sd     = sd(.data[[var]],     na.rm = TRUE),
      min    = min(.data[[var]],    na.rm = TRUE),
      max    = max(.data[[var]],    na.rm = TRUE),
    )
  print(table)
}

make_outlier <- function(var) {
  table <- project2_merged |>
    mutate(
      q1     = quantile(.data[[var]], .25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q3     = quantile(.data[[var]], .75, na.rm = TRUE),
      iqr    = q3 - q1,
      is_out = .data[[var]] < q1 - 1.5*iqr |
        .data[[var]] > q3 + 1.5*iqr
    ) |>
    filter(is_out) |>
    slice_max(abs(.data[[var]] -
                    median(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)), n = 5) |>
    select(name, Democracy, .data[[var]])
  print(table)
}


p1 <- make_plot("sanitation_access_pct", "Sanitation access (%)")
p2 <- make_plot("food_supply_kcal_per_person_day",  "Food supply (kcal/person/day)")
p3 <- make_plot("murder_deaths_per_100k", "Murder deaths per 100k")
p4 <- make_plot("child_deaths_per_100k",            "Child deaths per 100k")

t1 <- make_table("sanitation_access_pct")
t2 <- make_table("food_supply_kcal_per_person_day")
t3 <- make_table("murder_deaths_per_100k")
t4 <- make_table("child_deaths_per_100k")

o1 <- make_outlier("sanitation_access_pct")
o2 <- make_outlier("food_supply_kcal_per_person_day")
o3 <- make_outlier("murder_deaths_per_100k")
o4 <- make_outlier("child_deaths_per_100k")

```

## Variable 1: Sanitation Access

### Graph and description

```{r}
p1; t1; o1
```

### Stats and description

looking at the means of total sanitation access and by democracy status, non-democracies almost match the total mean (79%) while Democracies have almost 100% sanitation access. Implied in this analysis is that the samples by democracy status are significantly different and would be a good candidate for a single variable model. The 5 farthest outliers are all non-democracies and have below 20% sanitation access. 

## Variable 2: Food Supply

### Graph and description

```{r}
p2; t2; o2
```

### Stats and description

looking at the means of food supply by democracy status, non-democracies fall below the total mean (~2963 kcal/person/day) while Democracies fall above the total mean. Implied in this analysis is that the samples by democracy status are significantly different and would be a good candidate for a single variable model. There are no significant outliers in this comparison.

## Variable 3: Deaths from Murder

### Graph and description

```{r}
p3; t3; o3
```

### Stats and description
looking at the means of murders per capita by democracy status, both non-democracies and democracies fell around the total mean (~7.4 per capita) non-democracies had slightly higher murders per capita. Implied in this analysis is that the samples by democracy status appear to not be significantly different and should not be considered for the single variable model. There are 3 non-democratic outliers above 50 per capita and 2 democratic outliers above 20 per capita. 

## Variable 4: Child Deaths

### Graph and description

```{r}
p4; t4; o4
```

### Stats and description
looking at the means of child deaths per capita by democracy status, democracies fell below the total mean (~64 per capita) non-democracies had higher child deaths per capita. The two measn seem to be significantly different, and this variable is a good candidate for the single vairable model. All five farthest outliers are non-democracies and have above 240 child deaths per capita.

## Variable 5: Female Head of State

### Graph and description

```{r}
ggplot(project2_merged, aes(x = female_hos_binary, fill = Democracy)) + geom_bar(position = "fill") + labs( title = "Democracy Status by Female Head of State", x = "Female head of state (binary)", y = "Proportion", fill = "Democracy" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

#two way table
as.data.frame(table(project2_merged$female_hos_binary, project2_merged$Democracy))

#row proportions
as.data.frame(prop.table(table(project2_merged$female_hos_binary, project2_merged$Democracy), margin = 2))

#column proportions
as.data.frame(prop.table(table(project2_merged$female_hos_binary, project2_merged$Democracy)))

```

### Stats and description

The only state that survived into this merged dataset is Tanzania, being a one party state and a non-democracy. I am beginning to think the Female head of state category was poorly designed, maybe if the variable was redifined to mean "has had a female head of state" versus "has a female head of state". This variable does not have enough data for both democracies and non-democracies to be considered for the single variable model.
